selected_sections.heading: Premise
selected_sections.raw_wikitext: The series follows Marianne Sheridan, an affluent and isolated social outcast, and Connell Waldron, a popular, high-achieving student with [[anxiety]], as they begin a secretive relationship during their final days of secondary school in [[County Sligo]]. Connell's mother, Lorraine, is employed by Marianne's mother, Denise, as a cleaner.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Herman |first1=Alison |title='Normal People' Isn't a Story About Adults |url=https://www.theringer.com/tv/2020/4/29/21238820/normal-people-hulu-bbc-sally-rooney |website=The Ringer |date=29 April 2020 |access-date=24 November 2021 |archive-date=24 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211124052805/https://www.theringer.com/tv/2020/4/29/21238820/normal-people-hulu-bbc-sally-rooney |url-status=live }}</ref> Connell and Marianne's relationship becomes strained as their lives begin to change when they go on to attend [[Trinity College, Dublin|Trinity College]] in [[Dublin]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Normal People |date=2020-04-29 |type=Drama, Romance |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt9059760/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |others=Paul Mescal, Daisy Edgar-Jones, Desmond Eastwood |publisher=Element Pictures, British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC), Hulu Originals}}</ref>

selected_sections.heading: Critical response
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
The series was widely praised.  On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the series has a 91% rating, with an average score of 8.2/10 based on 91 reviews. The site's critical consensus reads, "Anchored by Daisy Edgar-Jones and Paul Mescal's vulnerable performances, ''Normal People'' is at once intimate and illuminating, beautifully translating the nuances of its source material."<ref>{{cite web |title=Normal People: Season 1 |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/normal_people/s01 |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media]] |access-date=8 March 2021 |archive-date=11 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201211024822/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/normal_people/s01 |url-status=live }}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the series has a score of 82 out of 100, based on reviews from 25 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref>{{cite web |title=Normal People |url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/normal-people/season-1 |website=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=14 February 2021 |archive-date=4 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210204142433/https://www.metacritic.com/tv/normal-people/season-1 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In a positive review for ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', [[Caroline Framke]] wrote: "With its trifecta of elegant writing, directing, and acting, ''Normal People'' is just as bleak and uncompromising as Rooney's novel, making you both crave and dread knowing—or perhaps more accurately, ''experiencing''—what happens."<ref>{{cite web |date= 22 April 2020 |last= Framke |first= Caroline |author-link= Caroline Framke |title= 'Normal People' on Hulu: TV Review |url= https://variety.com/2020/tv/reviews/normal-people-hulu-review-sally-rooney-1234587209/ |website= [[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date= 28 April 2020 |archive-date= 2 March 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210302213440/https://variety.com/2020/tv/reviews/normal-people-hulu-review-sally-rooney-1234587209/ |url-status= live }}</ref> [[NPR]]{{'}}s [[Linda Holmes (writer)|Linda Holmes]] praised the main cast's performances and their chemistry, writing, "[Mescal and Edgar-Jones] have the vulnerability it takes to maintain confidence. They've both figured out how to put a particular warmth in their eyes when they're able to find those connected moments, like a light that flips on. [Mescal] is a stunning talent for someone who is genuinely just starting out in television — it's a treat to see [the actors] work so well together".<ref>{{cite web|title='Normal People' Is A Love Story To Cherish|url=https://www.npr.org/2020/04/29/847617296/normal-people-is-a-love-story-to-cherish|website=NPR.org|date=29 April 2020|access-date=26 May 2020|last1=Holmes|first1=Linda|archive-date=29 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200429175608/https://www.npr.org/2020/04/29/847617296/normal-people-is-a-love-story-to-cherish|url-status=live}}</ref>

In a negative review, Jessa Crispin of ''[[The Guardian]]'' called the series "a gutless soap opera for millennials" and wrote the series is a "dull, tedious reworking of a romance plot as old as time". Crispin also criticized its unrealistic depiction of university freshmen, casting of older actors to play teenagers, and lack of depth, writing, "[''Normal People''] analyzes itself with offhand comments so you don't have to do any thinking."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2020/may/05/sally-rooney-normal-people-hulu-bbc-soap-opera|title=Normal People is little more than a gutless soap opera for millennials|publisher=The Guardian|date=May 5, 2020|accessdate=August 20, 2025|first=Jessa|last=Crispin}}</ref> In another negative review, Matt Fagerholm of ''[[RogerEbert.com]]'' compared ''Normal People'' to "being stuck on a bad date that refuses to end", criticizing its writing, Mescal's casting, and its "cowardly" and "unforgivable" characters, calling Marianne a "despairing addition to an array of submissive heroines routinely defined by the men in their lives" and concluded that the series is "a frustrating, fractured romance between an inarticulate weakling and a woman who deserves much better".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/streaming/hulus-normal-people-has-all-the-appeal-of-a-bad-date-that-refuses-to-end|title=Hulu's Normal People Has All the Appeal of a Bad Date That Refuses to End|publisher=RogerEbert|date=April 23, 2020|accessdate=August 20, 2025|first=Matt|last=Fagerholm}}</ref>

The series received controversy for its nudity and sex scenes:<ref>{{cite web |title="Normal People: we need to discuss this BBC show's portrayal of sex and consent" |url=https://www.stylist.co.uk/life/normal-people-sex-scenes-consent-porn-marianne-connell-daisy-edgar-jones-paul-mescal/383681 |website=[[Stylist (magazine)|Stylist]] |date=27 April 2020 |access-date=3 May 2020 |archive-date=13 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200513061308/https://www.stylist.co.uk/life/normal-people-sex-scenes-consent-porn-marianne-connell-daisy-edgar-jones-paul-mescal/383681 |url-status=live }}</ref>  while the work of [[Ita O'Brien]] as the show's [[intimacy coordinator]] was praised,<ref>{{cite web |date= 1 May 2020 |last= Kaufman |first= Amy |title= This is how 'Normal People' made some of TV's steamiest sex scenes |url= https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/tv/story/2020-05-01/normal-people-sex-hulu-intimacy-coordinator |website= [[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date= 3 May 2020 |archive-date= 3 May 2020 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200503015612/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/tv/story/2020-05-01/normal-people-sex-hulu-intimacy-coordinator |url-status= live }}</ref> some viewers called in to complain on ''[[Liveline]]'', arguing the nudity was excessive or inappropriate.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://metro.co.uk/2020/05/01/what-see-porno-normal-people-immoral-sex-scenes-spark-major-debate-irish-radio-12639380/|title='It's what you'd see in a porno': Normal People 'immoral' sex scenes spark major debate on Irish radio|journal=Metro|first=Emma|last=Kelly|date=1 May 2020|access-date=13 May 2020|archive-date=17 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200517140228/https://metro.co.uk/2020/05/01/what-see-porno-normal-people-immoral-sex-scenes-spark-major-debate-irish-radio-12639380/|url-status=live}}</ref> selected_sections.heading: Viewing figures
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
''Normal People'' reportedly gave [[BBC Three]] its best ever week on [[BBC iPlayer|iPlayer]] (26 April to 3 May), receiving over 16.2 million programme requests across the 12 episodes, about 5 million of which were from 16- to 34-year-olds, and bringing BBC Three requests up to 21.8 million, doubling the previous record of 10.8 million from the release of the first series of ''[[Killing Eve]]''. Seventy per cent of BBC Three requests that week were for ''Normal People'' and a quarter had finished all 12 episodes.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://deadline.com/2020/05/normal-people-scores-16m-views-bbc-iplayer-1202926180/|title='Normal People' Scores 16M Views In Its First Week On BBC iPlayer|journal=Deadline|first=Jake|last=Kanter|date=5 May 2020|access-date=5 May 2020|archive-date=29 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200829130440/https://deadline.com/2020/05/normal-people-scores-16m-views-bbc-iplayer-1202926180/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.rapidtvnews.com/2020050558448/normal-people-takes-bbc-three-to-its-best-week-ever.html|title=Normal People takes BBC Three to its best week ever|journal=Rapid TV News|first=Joseph|last=O'Halloran|date=5 May 2020|access-date=5 May 2020|archive-date=2 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302222115/https://www.rapidtvnews.com/2020050558448/normal-people-takes-bbc-three-to-its-best-week-ever.html|url-status=live}}</ref> It became the most-streamed series of the year on the BBC, with 62.7 million views from April to November 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/news/on-demand/2020-12-08/normal-people-popular-bbc-iplayer-2020-news/ |title=Normal People biggest series on BBC iPlayer with 62.7m |first=Patrick |last=McLennan |date=8 December 2020 |work=Radio Times |access-date=25 December 2020 |archive-date=10 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201210090041/https://www.radiotimes.com/news/on-demand/2020-12-08/normal-people-popular-bbc-iplayer-2020-news/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The first two episodes were reported to have been watched on [[RTÉ One]] by an average of 371,000 viewers with an additional 19,000 on RTÉ One +1 and 301,000 streams on [[RTÉ Player]], becoming the most watched opening of a drama series on RTÉ Player. Thirty per cent of 15- to 34-year-olds watching TV were watching ''Normal People''.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://extra.ie/2020/05/05/entertainment/movies-tv/normal-people-big-hit-rte|title=Normal People is a big hit with viewers as over 370,000 tune in|journal=Extra.ie|first=Ali|last=Condon|date=5 May 2020|access-date=5 May 2020|archive-date=12 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812033705/https://extra.ie/2020/05/05/entertainment/movies-tv/normal-people-big-hit-rte|url-status=live}}</ref> The finale had over 319,000 viewers, 33% of the total RTÉ audience and 20% increase over the previous week. In June 2020, it was reported that ''Normal People'' had garnered over 3 million views on [[RTÉ Player]], breaking the previous record for the streaming service of 1.2 million, which was held by the fourth series of ''[[Love/Hate (TV series)|Love/Hate]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.irishpost.com/entertainment/normal-people-smashes-rte-player-record-to-become-most-watched-show-ever-186206|title=Normal People smashes RTÉ Player record to become most-watched show ever|journal=The Irish Post|first=Rachael|last=O'Connor|date=4 June 2020|access-date=29 July 2020|archive-date=9 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200709123034/https://www.irishpost.com/entertainment/normal-people-smashes-rte-player-record-to-become-most-watched-show-ever-186206|url-status=live}}</ref>

Speaking on the series' popularity, Prathyush Parasuraman of ''[[Film Companion]]'' wrote: "Rarely have I seen the sort of cultural dialogue that I saw [from] the release of ''Normal People''."<ref>{{cite web|last=Parasuraman|first=Pratyush|date=5 January 2021|title=Normal People Review|url=https://www.filmcompanion.in/streaming/normal-people-lionsgate-play-is-the-millennial-mecca-of-love-and-lust-sally-rooney-daisy-edgar-jones-paul-mescal|access-date=6 January 2021|work=Film Companion|archive-date=5 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210105110715/https://www.filmcompanion.in/streaming/normal-people-lionsgate-play-is-the-millennial-mecca-of-love-and-lust-sally-rooney-daisy-edgar-jones-paul-mescal/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The first season received positive reviews. On the [[review aggregator]] website [[Rotten Tomatoes]] 87% 100 reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7.7/10. selected_sections.heading: Season 2
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
[[File:Pall Mall - Project Gutenberg eText 14315.jpg|thumb|[[Pall-mall]] features as a [[pastime]] for the Bridgerton siblings in the [[Bridgerton season 2|second season]]]]
The second season received positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 78% of 95 critic reviews are positive with an average rating of 7.1/10. The website's critics consensus states, "The risqué thrill may have faded, but ''Bridgerton'' remains a compulsive episode-turner in this delightful sophomore season."<ref name="S2RT">{{cite Rotten Tomatoes |title=Bridgerton |id=bridgerton |type=tv |season=2 |access-date=July 23, 2024}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Metacritic gave the series a weighted average score of 70 out of 100 based on 32 reviews, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="S2MC">{{cite Metacritic |title=Bridgerton |id=bridgerton |type=tv |season=2 |access-date=April 6, 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref name="hollywoodreporter1">{{cite web |last1=Porter |first1=Rick |date=March 29, 2022 |title=''Bridgerton'' Season 2 Sets Netflix Opening Weekend Viewing Record (Exclusive) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/bridgerton-season-2-netflix-record-viewing-1235121606/ |access-date=April 30, 2022 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-date=April 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220422011241/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/bridgerton-season-2-netflix-record-viewing-1235121606/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Kristen Baldwin of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' gave the series an A−, writing, "With a second season that's more clever, moving, and emotionally complex than the first, this period drama ... proves that it's not just a titillating trifle."<ref>{{cite magazine |date=March 20, 2022 |first=Kristen |last=Baldwin |title='Bridgerton' season 2 review: No Duke? No problem! |url=https://ew.com/tv/tv-reviews/bridgerton-season-2-review-netflix/ |access-date=April 13, 2022 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |language=en |archive-date=April 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220413131629/https://ew.com/tv/tv-reviews/bridgerton-season-2-review-netflix/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]''{{'s}} Angie Hahn echoed the sentiment, describing the season as "older and wiser" than its predecessor's "rampant horniness", with an effective central romance that prioritized "a meeting of minds, played out over quick-witted arguments outside [[ballroom]]s and vicious competition during a friendly family game of [[pall-mall]]".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Han |first1=Angie |date=March 20, 2022 |title=Netflix's 'Bridgerton' Season 2: TV Review |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-reviews/bridgerton-season-2-tv-review-1235114578/ |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-date=April 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220413135147/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-reviews/bridgerton-season-2-tv-review-1235114578/ |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Peter Travers]] of [[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] praised the season writing, "Kudos to season two for digging deeper into the emotional lives of its characters and continuing the [[Color-blind casting|colorblind casting]] that creates a [[utopia]] in which diversity is so ingrained it's hardly worth a mention."<ref>{{cite web |title=Review: 'Bridgerton Season 2' brims over with smoldering romance and unexpected edge |url=https://goodmorningamerica.com/culture/story/review-bridgerton-season-brims-smoldering-romance-unexpected-edge-83636737 |access-date=April 24, 2022 |website=ABC News |language=en |archive-date=May 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220506190635/https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/culture/story/review-bridgerton-season-brims-smoldering-romance-unexpected-edge-83636737 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Alison Herman of [[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]] commented that Season 1 is "sexy without quite being erotic" while "Season 2 is the reverse. There's not a lot of sex, but in the crackling chemistry and relentless self-denial that defines Anthony and Kate's dynamic, there's plenty of [[eroticism]]."<ref>{{cite news |last=Herman |first=Alison |date=March 28, 2022 |title='Bridgerton' Season 2 Understands That Romance Is Hotter Than Sex |url=https://www.theringer.com/tv/2022/3/28/22999145/bridgerton-season-2-review-anthony-kate-sex-romance |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=The Ringer |language=en |archive-date=April 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220413141719/https://www.theringer.com/tv/2022/3/28/22999145/bridgerton-season-2-review-anthony-kate-sex-romance |url-status=live}}</ref> Emma Clarke of ''[[The Independent]]'' argued that, "it is precisely the lack of [[Human sexual activity|physicality]] that makes this season (of the show and of [[courtship]]) so... well, sexy."<ref>{{cite news |date=April 12, 2022 |title=Opinion: Bridgerton season two's lack of sex scenes makes it all the hotter |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/voices/bridgerton-s2-netflix-sex-scenes-kate-anthony-b2054040.html |access-date=April 13, 2022 |newspaper=The Independent |language=en |archive-date=April 12, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220412104658/https://www.independent.co.uk/voices/bridgerton-s2-netflix-sex-scenes-kate-anthony-b2054040.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Scott Bryan of the [[BBC]] wrote that the season serves as an antidote to the "always static, laboured and slow" period dramas, adding that it comes with "real energy, it feels so modern (even though it is set in the past) and even though it feels extravagant, it doesn't feel too [[highbrow]]. It is refreshingly accessible."<ref>{{cite web |date=March 23, 2022 |title=Bridgerton Season Two: What the Must Watch reviewers think |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/5live/entries/de847cb9-c795-4b7e-8042-a72521c9c962 |access-date=April 14, 2022 |website=BBC Radio 5 Live |language=en |archive-date=April 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220414213051/https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/5live/entries/de847cb9-c795-4b7e-8042-a72521c9c962 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Kevin Fallon of ''[[The Daily Beast]]'', elaborating on Bailey's "exquisite lead performance", wrote that "he has an exceptional ability to carry his angst, pain, and guilt with him without bogging down things into a somber drag."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fallon |first=Kevin |date=March 25, 2022 |title=Even With Fewer Butts, 'Bridgerton' Is Still Worth Watching |work=The Daily Beast |url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/even-with-fewer-butts-jonathan-bailey-makes-bridgerton-season-2-worth-watching |url-status=live |access-date=May 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220430052255/https://www.thedailybeast.com/even-with-fewer-butts-jonathan-bailey-makes-bridgerton-season-2-worth-watching |archive-date=April 30, 2022}}</ref> ''[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]''{{'s}} Anita Singh wrote that Bailey "brings more soul to the role of Lord Bridgerton than Page ever did with the Duke",<ref>{{Cite news |last=Singh |first=Anita |date=March 25, 2022 |title=Bridgerton, series 2, review: the Regency romp is back, but why have they dialled down the sex? selected_sections.heading: Season 3
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
The third season received positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 87% of 79 critic reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7.0/10. The website's critics consensus states, "The hot goss in London remains juicy as ever in ''Bridgerton''{{'s}} third season, which benefits tremendously from Nicola Coughlan and Luke Newton's endearing chemistry."<ref name="S3RT">{{cite Rotten Tomatoes |title=Bridgerton |id=bridgerton |type=tv |season=3 |access-date=July 23, 2024}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Metacritic gave the series a weighted average score of 69 out of 100 based on 26 reviews, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="S3MC">{{cite Metacritic |title=Bridgerton |id=bridgerton |type=tv |season=3 |access-date=May 23, 2024}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Aramide Tinubu of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' praised Coughlan and Newton's chemistry, noting that while they have always had a "beautiful rapport", "there is something about seeing the bond between Colin and Penelope transform from comfortably platonic to yearning and passionate that elevates this journey."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tinubu |first=Aramide |date=May 16, 2024 |title=Polin's Love Story in 'Bridgerton' Season 3 Part 1 Delivers Glow-Ups, Deception and Some Super Sultry Moments: TV Review |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/reviews/bridgerton-season-3-part-1-review-1235997265/ |access-date=February 3, 2025 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> Tinubu also found part 2 of Season 3 "as a gem in the franchise".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tinubu |first=Aramide |date=June 13, 2024 |title='Bridgerton' Season 3 Part 2 Is the Most Fascinating Chapter of the Franchise Yet: TV Review |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/reviews/bridgerton-season-3-part-2-review-1236015585/ |access-date=February 3, 2025 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> David Opie of ''[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]'' praised part 2's mirror scene as "the most beautiful sex scene this show has ever depicted" and featuring "some of the finest acting seen in ''Bridgerton'' yet".<ref name="Empire-2024">{{Cite web |date=June 14, 2024 |title=Bridgerton: Season 3, Part 2 |url=https://www.empireonline.com/tv/reviews/bridgerton-season-3-part-2/ |access-date=February 3, 2025 |website=Empire |language=en}}</ref> Further, Opie found that "Season 3 ends with the show's strongest episodes yet" and that ''Bridgerton'' has cemented itself as "the rare Netflix success story that's just as well made as it is widely watched".<ref name="Empire-2024" /> Rachel Aroesti of ''[[The Guardian]]'' credited ''Bridgerton'' Season 3 of benefiting from having two seasons under its belt in portraying the most "captivating courtship yet", and praised the dynamic between Colin and Penelope, partly attributing it to Coughlan's "sensational" acting.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Aroesti |first=Rachel |date=May 16, 2024 |title=Bridgerton season three review – still unbearably sexy |url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/article/2024/may/16/bridgerton-season-three-review-still-unbearably-sexy |access-date=February 3, 2025 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Alyssa Mora of ''[[IGN]]'' describes Coughlan and Newton's chemistry as "undeniable", and Coughlan's talent as "manag[ing] to take center stage".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mora |first=Alyssa |date=July 24, 2024 |title=Bridgerton Season 3 Is Just Fine – That's Why It's So Frustrating |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/bridgerton-season-3-review-netflix |access-date=February 3, 2025 |website=IGN |language=en}}</ref>

Katie Rosseinsky of ''The Independent'' called Coughlan "the true diamond of the season", and praised her powerhouse performance alongside Jessie.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rosseinsky |first=Katie |date=June 14, 2024 |title=Bridgerton season three part two review: The wheels are starting to come off the carriage |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/bridgerton-season-3-part-2-review-ending-polin-b2562511.html |access-date=February 3, 2025 |work=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> Carly Lane of ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]'' also called Coughlan the "true diamond" of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lane |first=Carly |date=May 16, 2024 |title='Bridgerton' Season 3 Review: of ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' praised Coughlan's Penelope as the "series’ most compelling protagonist to date", and Coughlan for the "vividness and sensitivity" in which she portrayed Penelope's transformation.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berman |first=Judy |date=May 16, 2024 |title=Three Seasons In, 'Bridgerton' Finally Has a Great Heroine Hollywood Reporter'' noted that "while the latest chapter faithfully delivers on everything we’ve come to expect from this world [...] it's also the first in which the formula feels more familiar than selected_sections.heading: Season 4
selected_sections.raw_wikitext: The fourth season received positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 81% of 58 critics' reviews are positive. The website's critics consensus states, "Taking a page out of a fairytale, ''Bridgerton'' season four excels at selling a fantasy that, no matter how predictable, is as sweet, steamy, and engrossing as ever."<ref name="S4RT">{{Cite web|title=Bridgerton: Season 4 |website=Rotten Tomatoes|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/bridgerton/s04|access-date=March 5, 2026|language=en}}</ref> [[Metacritic]] gave the season a weighted average score of 65 out of 100 based on 23 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="S4MC">{{Cite web|title=Bridgerton season 4 Reviews|url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/bridgerton/season-4/|website=Metacritic|access-date=January 30, 2026|language=en}}</ref>

selected_sections.heading: Season 2
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
Season 2 premiered on March 25, 2022, and debuted number one in 92 countries on the platform. It was also the most viewed show on United States [[Television|television screens]] for three weeks per [[Nielsen Media Research]].<ref name="hollywoodreporter1" /> Season 2 amassed 193 million viewing hours in its opening weekend, the highest opening for any English-language Netflix series at the time.<ref name="hollywoodreporter1" /> It also broke the record for most viewed English-language series in a single week at that time, with 251.74 million viewing hours from March 28 to April 3. The first season also re-entered Netflix's top ten in second place.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://deadline.com/2022/04/bridgerton-season-2-sets-netflix-viewing-record-english-language-series-1234994885/ |title='Bridgerton' Season 2 Sets Netflix Ratings Record For English-Language Series |magazine=Deadline |first=Peter |last=White |date=April 6, 2022 |access-date=April 5, 2022 |archive-date=April 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220405235208/https://deadline.com/2022/04/bridgerton-season-2-sets-netflix-viewing-record-english-language-series-1234994885/ |url-status=live}}</ref> By April 19, ''Bridgerton''{{'}}s second season had overtaken its predecessor as the [[List of most-watched Netflix original programming|most watched English-language television series on Netflix]] at the time with 627.11 million hours viewed since its March 25, 2022, launch.<ref>{{cite web |last=Maas |first=Jennifer |date=April 19, 2022 |title=''Bridgerton'' Season 2 Overtakes Season 1 in Netflix's All-Time TV Rankings |url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/bridgerton-season-2-beats-season-1-netflix-viewership-ratings-1235235479/ |access-date=April 19, 2022 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-date=April 19, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220419192714/https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/bridgerton-season-2-beats-season-1-netflix-viewership-ratings-1235235479/ |url-status=live}}</ref> This viewing numbers went up to 656.16 million by the 28-day mark.<ref>{{cite web |title=Season 2 has officially cemented its place as the #1 English TV series on Netflix. One month after its premiere on Netflix, the secrets of Lady Whistledown have amassed a whopping 656.16M hours viewed. |url=https://about.netflix.com/en/news/top-10-week-of-april-18-anatomy-of-a-scandal-is-the-weeks-most-viewed-title |access-date=April 26, 2022 |website=About Netflix |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220626083559/https://about.netflix.com/en/news/top-10-week-of-april-18-anatomy-of-a-scandal-is-the-weeks-most-viewed-title |archive-date=June 26, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Nielsen Media Research]], analyzing the 2.55 billion minutes viewed on United States television screens in the first three days of season 2's availability (double all others across streamers for the week of March 21), characterized ''Bridgerton''{{'s}} audience as "diverse and broad". The firm found one third of viewers to be Hispanic or African American and an even split in popularity across the 18–34, 35–49, and 50–64 age groups at 25% each. The only exception was gender parity, with 76% of the audience reported to be female.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.tvline.com/ratings/bridgerton-season-2-tops-nielsen-streaming-top-10-chart-1234822226/ |title=Bridgerton Dominates Nielsen Top 10 Chart With Season 2 Release, Audience That Is 76 selected_sections.heading: Season 3
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
In 2023, between seasons 2 and 3, Netflix rolled out a new, different method of counting viewership, which is to divide the number of hours watched by a show's runtime. The platform also expanded the measurement window from 28 days to 91 days.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://deadline.com/2023/06/netflix-changes-viewership-ratings-shakeup-all-time-most-popular-tv-wednesday-stranger-things-4-queen-charlotte-1235420897/ |title=Netflix Adjusts Viewership Metric, Prompting Shakeups Among All-Time Most Popular Lists; 'Wednesday' Overtakes 'Stranger Things 4' & 'Queen Charlotte' Remains In Play For TV |magazine=Deadline |first=Katie |last=Campione |date=June 20, 2023 |access-date=May 21, 2024 |archive-date=May 10, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240510091253/https://deadline.com/2023/06/netflix-changes-viewership-ratings-shakeup-all-time-most-popular-tv-wednesday-stranger-things-4-queen-charlotte-1235420897/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Under this new method of measurement, season 3 part 1, which had 220 minutes of runtime, received 45.05 million views in its first week,<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/bridgerton-season-3-viewership-netflix-madame-web-1235926159/ |title='Bridgerton' Season 3 Captures Netflix Top 10 Crown With Impressive Debut Weekend Viewership; 'Madame Web' Takes No. 2 In Film |magazine=Deadline |first=Katie |last=Campione |date=May 21, 2024 |access-date=May 21, 2024 |archive-date=May 21, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521223138/https://deadline.com/2024/05/bridgerton-season-3-viewership-netflix-madame-web-1235926159/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and then 25.3 million views in its second week,<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.thewrap.com/bridgerton-season-3-atlas-netflix-viewership/ |title='Bridgerton' Season 3 Reign Continues as Netflix's Most-Watched Series of the Week With 25.3 Million Views |magazine=The Wrap |first=Loree |last=Seitz |date=May 28, 2024 |access-date=May 29, 2024 |archive-date=May 29, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240529080155/https://www.thewrap.com/bridgerton-season-3-atlas-netflix-viewership/ |url-status=live}}</ref> 11.6 million in its third,<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/netflix-top-10-streaming-ratings-1235697082/ |title=Netflix Top 10: 'Dancing for the Devil: The 7M TikTok Cult' Debuts in Second Place as 'Bridgerton' Streak Continues |magazine=Variety |first=Selome |last=Hailu |date=June 4, 2024 |access-date=June 10, 2024 |archive-date=January 31, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240131025243/https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/netflix-top-10-streaming-ratings-1235697082/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and 6.9 million in its fourth. After season 3 part 2 debuted (based on 480 minutes of runtime), the overall season received 28 million views that debut week,<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.thewrap.com/bridgerton-season-3-part-2-netflix-viewership-ratings/ |title='Bridgerton' Season 3 Dominates Netflix's Most-Watched TV List After Part 2 Debut With 28 Million Views |magazine=The Wrap |first=Loree |last=Seitz |date=June 18, 2024 |access-date=June 19, 2024 |archive-date=June 19, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240619040047/https://www.thewrap.com/bridgerton-season-3-part-2-netflix-viewership-ratings/ |url-status=live}}</ref> 16.5 million views the following week,<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/netflix-top-10-jessica-alba-190000796.html |title=Netflix Top 10: Jessica Alba's 'Trigger Warning' Is the Most-Watched Title of the Week, 'Bridgerton' Leads TV Titles |website=Yahoo Entertainment |via=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=June 25, 2024 |first=Selome |last=Hailu |access-date=June 28, 2024}}</ref> 6.6 million views the third week, and 4 million the fourth.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://advanced-television.com/2024/07/03/all-bridgerton-seasons-on-netflixs-most-popular-tv-list/ |title=All Bridgerton seasons on Netflix's Most Popular TV List |website=Advanced Television |date=July 3, 2024 |access-date=July 9, 2024}}</ref>

Season 3 part 1 recorded the show's biggest opening weekend to date with 165.2 million views (on 220 minutes of runtime).<ref name="Porter-2024">{{Cite web |last=Porter |first=Rick |date=May 21, 2024 |title='Bridgerton' Season 3 Scores Series Best Opening in Netflix Rankings |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/bridgerton-season-3-biggest-opening-netflix-ratings-1235905470/ |access-date=February 2, 2025 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref> At the time, Season 3 also recorded the highest single weekly view count for any Netflix series, regardless of language, since Netflix started the list in June 2023.<ref name="Porter-2024" /> On July 2, 2024, Season 3 became Netflix's tenth biggest English-language series ever with 91.9 million views so far.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hailu |first=Selome |date=July 2, 2024 |title='Bridgerton' Season 3 Becomes Netflix's 10th Biggest English-Language Series Ever With 91.9 Million Views So Far |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/netflix-top-10-streaming-ratings-june-24-1236063757/ |access-date=February 2, 2025 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> As of January 1, 2025, Season 3 was sixth in Netflix's top-10 all-time list, for any language, with 846.5 million hours viewed/106 million views.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tassi |first=Paul |title='Squid Game' Season 2 Breaks Yet Another Netflix Record |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/paultassi/2025/01/01/squid-game-season-2-breaks-yet-another-netflix-record/ |access-date=February 3, 2025 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

Season 3 became the second most watched series on Netflix during the first half of 2024, with 92 million views.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/netflix-engagement-report-january-june-2024.html |title=The Limits of a Twice-Yearly Netflix Viewing Report |website=Vulture |date=September 19, 2024 |access-date=September 23, 2024}}</ref> Season 3 has the second-highest viewing figures for streaming in 2024, with 11 billion minutes of watch time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 Year-end Film & TV Report |url=https://luminatedata.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/luminate-ftv-year-end-report-2024.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250128115408/https://luminatedata.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Luminate-FTV-Year-End-Report-2024.pdf |archive-date=January 28, 2025 |access-date=February 2, 2025 |website=Luminate}}</ref> According to Nielsen, ''Bridgerton'' was the most-streamed original series of 2024 with 21.42 billion minutes viewed, with Season 3 accounting for 56% of those views.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Porter |first=Rick |date=January 27, 2025 |title=The Year of 'Bluey': Kids' Favorite Dominates 2024 Year-End Streaming Chart |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/bluey-bridgerton-2024-year-end-streaming-charts-1236119192/ |access-date=February 2, 2025 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Adgate |first=Brad |title='Bluey,' 'Bridgerton' And 'Moana' Were Among The Most Streamed In 2024 |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/bradadgate/2025/01/27/bluey-bridgerton--moana-were-among-the-most-streamed-in-2024/ |access-date=February 2, 2025 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

selected_sections.heading: Season 4
selected_sections.raw_wikitext: Season 4 is the first installment in the franchise not to reach Netflix's all-time Top 10 most-watched shows within the platform's 91-day measurement window.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ingham |first=Alexandria |date=June 4, 2026 |title='Bridgerton' Season 4 Marks a Disappointing First for the Franchise on Netflix |url=https://parade.com/tv/bridgerton-season-4-marks-a-disappointing-first-for-the-franchise-on-netflix |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260606125046/https://parade.com/tv/bridgerton-season-4-marks-a-disappointing-first-for-the-franchise-on-netflix |archive-date=June 6, 2026 |access-date=June 9, 2026 |work=Parade |language=en}}</ref> Season 4 is estimated to have finished with 92–95 million views.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2, 2026 |title='Bridgerton' Season 4 Becomes the First Season to Miss Netflix's All-Time Top 10 List |url=https://www.whats-on-netflix.com/news/bridgerton-season-4-becomes-the-first-season-to-miss-netflixs-all-time-top-10-list/ |access-date=June 9, 2026 |website=What's on Netflix |language=en}}</ref>

Fashion and interior design trends influenced or made popular by the series have been dubbed "[[Regencycore]]" or "the ''Bridgerton'' effect".<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Joyner |first=Lisa |date=March 25, 2022 |title=What is Regencycore? 9 ways you can tap into the rising interior trend |url=https://www.countryliving.com/uk/homes-interiors/interiors/a35276461/regencycore-trend-bridgerton/ |magazine=Country Living |access-date=April 6, 2022 |archive-date=April 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406000811/https://www.countryliving.com/uk/homes-interiors/interiors/a35276461/regencycore-trend-bridgerton/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Lyst'' reported an increase in searches for items such as [[corset]]s, headpieces, and elbow-length gloves after the series' premiere. The series' first two female leads, Daphne and Kate, were also linked to a popularity in the colors sky blue and lilac respectively.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=February 26, 2021 |title='Bridgerton', TikTok, and the revival of 'Regencycore' fashion |url=https://www.inputmag.com/style/netflix-bridgerton-regencycore-fashion-dresses-corsets-tiktok-trend |magazine=Input |access-date=April 6, 2022 |archive-date=April 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406102547/https://www.inputmag.com/style/netflix-bridgerton-regencycore-fashion-dresses-corsets-tiktok-trend After season three part one, "The Carriage Scene" became a standalone viral moment for the series, and was individually nominated for a [[British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment|BAFTA P&O Cruises Memorable Moment Award]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 27, 2025 |title=One of the 'raunchiest TV moments of 2024' could win a Bafta |url=https://metro.co.uk/2025/03/27/one-raunchiest-tv-moments-2024-win-a-bafta-22804358/ |access-date=August 24, 2025 |website=Metro |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2025 Nominations revealed for the P&O Cruises Memorable Moment Award |url=https://www.bafta.org/media-centre/press-releases/2025-nominations-po-cruises-memorable-moment/ |access-date=August 24, 2025 |website=Bafta |language=en}}</ref> and an Edinburgh TV Award for TV Moment of the Year, winning the latter award on August 21, 2025, at the [[Edinburgh International Television Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 22, 2025 |title=Nicola Coughlan wins TV Moment of the Year |url=https://www.rte.ie/entertainment/2025/0822/1529609-nicola-coughlan-wins-tv-moment-of-the-year/ |publisher=RTÉ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Cormack |first=Morgan |title=RadioTimes.com TV 100 2025 – the full list |magazine=Radio Times |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/tv-100-2025-full-list/ |access-date=August 24, 2025 |language=en-GB}}</ref> The romantic moment between season three leads Colin and Penelope would go on to be directly referenced in episode 3 of ''[[Emily in Paris]]'' season four when character Mindy Chen jokes "Oh! Someone's living out their horny Bridgerton fantasies" when she sees a carriage rocking outside of a ball.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mercuri |first=Monica |title='Emily In Paris' Director Unpacks Season 4's Love Triangle, Masquerade Ball And 'Bridgerton' Nods |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/monicamercuri/2024/08/16/emily-in-paris-director-unpacks-season-4s-love-triangle-masquerade-ball-and-bridgerton-nods/ |access-date=August 24, 2025 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> ''Bridgerton''{{'s}} carriage scene's social impact also inspired comparisons between the friends to lovers storylines of ''Bridgerton''{{'s}} "Polin" and ''[[The Gilded Age (TV series)|The Gilded Age]]''{{'}}s "Larian" when a carriage scene was used in advertisements for ''The Gilded Age'' season three in summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2, 2025 |title='Gilded Age' Fans Spotted A 'Bridgerton'-esque Detail In The Season 3 Trailer |url=https://www.bustle.com/entertainment/the-gilded-age-season-3-trailer-larry-marian-carriage-scene |access-date=August 24, 2025 |website=Bustle |language=en}}</ref> In October 2024, Netflix would use "The Carriage Scene" with the tagline "What a Ride" and the timestamp of the scene as the advertisement to launch their "Moments" feature to the Netflix mobile app.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 28, 2024 |title=Netflix Used Sexy 'Bridgerton' Scene To Launch A Helpful New Feature |url=https://uproxx.com/tv/netflix-moments-bridgerton-carriage-scene/ |access-date=August 24, 2025 |website=UPROXX |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Maas |first=Jennifer |date=October 28, 2024 |title=Netflix Adds 'Moments' Feature Allowing Users to Easily Share Favorite Scenes (EXCLUSIVE) |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/netflix-moments-feature-favorite-scenes-1236192331/ |access-date=August 24, 2025 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> The orchestral cover of "[[Give Me Everything]]" arranged by Archer Marsh that was used to score The Carriage Scene also contributed to the scene's virality on the social media app [[TikTok]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seitz |first=Loree |date=May 22, 2024 |title=Pitbull Responds to Viral 'Bridgerton' Carriage Scene Cover: 'Music Is the International Language' |url=https://www.thewrap.com/bridgerton-season-3-pitbull-cover-carriage-scene-reaction/ |access-date=August 24, 2025 |website=The Wrap |language=en-US}}</ref> The original artist [[Pitbull (rapper)|Pitbull]] later took to Instagram to post the scene with the caption "This again shows the world how music is the international language that transcends over boundaries more so how a hit song can remain timeless."<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 22, 2024 |title=Pitbull loves the 'Bridgerton' strings cover as much as everyone else |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/pitbull-bridgerton-strings-cover-response-rcna153571 |access-date=August 24, 2025 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref>

Netflix tripled its brand partnerships for season 3, and the Queen's Ball expanded to a dozen cities in addition to an afternoon tea event at [[the Lanesborough]] in London. ''[[The Wrap]]'' called ''Bridgerton'' fans a "ripe testing group" for this international merchandising and live-experience strategy from Netflix, comparing it to the likes of [[Disney]] and [[Universal Studios, Inc.|Universal]] franchises.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.thewrap.com/bridgerton-business-value-netflix-merch-product-partnerships/ |title=The Business of 'Bridgerton': How Netflix Is Capitalizing on One of Its Biggest Hits |magazine=The Wrap |first=Loree |last=Seitz |date=June 27, 2024 |access-date=June 28, 2024}}</ref>

selected_sections.heading: Gender
Race
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
[[File:Golda rosheuvel bts.jpg|thumb|305x305px|Queen Charlotte in the series as portrayed by [[Golda Rosheuvel]]]]
A notable, modernized twist on the show is the diverse cast of characters. Straying from the source novels, Van Dusen "used Queen Charlotte as a centerpiece to weave racial equality in the show."<ref name="ShondalandS1" /> With Queen Charlotte cast as a Black woman, Van Dusen explains, "Could she have used her power to elevate other people of color in society? Could she have given them titles and lands and dukedoms?"<ref name="Tillet-2021">{{Cite news |last=Tillet |first=Salamishah |date=January 5, 2021 |title='Bridgerton' Takes On Race. But Its Core Is Escapism. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/05/arts/television/bridgerton-race-netflix.html |access-date=May 3, 2024 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=March 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210316073403/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/05/arts/television/bridgerton-race-netflix.html |url-status=live}}</ref> 

When Simon Basset rejects the idea of pursuing Daphne Bridgerton, Lady Danbury explains that love conquers all, using Queen Charlotte and King George as an example of how their marriage had changed society.<ref>{{cite episode |title=An Affair of Honor |series=Bridgerton |series-link=Bridgerton |last1=McDonald |first1=Abby |last2= |first2= |network=Netflix |date=December 2020 |season=1 |number=4 |first3= |last3= |first4= |last4=}}</ref> Simon counters that, even though Queen Charlotte is currently in power, "Black progress is fragile and dependent on the whims of whichever white king is in charge."<ref name="Tillet-2021" />

selected_sections.heading: Literature
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
''Bridgerton'' also explores the "power of the written word",{{attribution needed|date=March 2026}} with authors such as Lady Whistledown having immense influence over the social season with her Society Papers. Similar to how media can strongly sway public opinion, Van Dusen makes the statement that "social media is kind of like a modern-day corset".{{attribution needed|date=March 2026}}<ref name="ShondalandS1" />

Throughout the show, Lady Whistledown releases Society Papers that comment on notable figures during the social season, whether it be praising them or airing out their secrets. The pamphlets' influence is enough to sway even Queen Charlotte herself, who seeks to find the author of the Society Papers in order to shut them down.<ref>{{cite episode |title=The Duke and I |series=Bridgerton |series-link=Bridgerton |last1=Mitchell |first1=Joy C. |last2= |first2= |network=Netflix |date=December 2020 |season=1 |number=5 |first3= |last3= |first4= |last4=Bostick}}</ref>

'''''Heartstopper''''' is a British [[Coming-of-age story|coming-of-age]] [[Romantic comedy|romantic]] [[comedy-drama]] television series created and written by [[Alice Oseman]] for [[Netflix]], based on her [[Heartstopper (graphic novel)|webcomic and graphic novel series of the same name]]. Starring [[Kit Connor]] and [[Joe Locke]] as [[Nick Nelson (Heartstopper)|Nick Nelson]] and [[Charlie Spring]], it follows two teenagers whose friendship at Truham Grammar School develops into a romantic relationship. Its ensemble cast includes [[William Gao]], [[Yasmin Finney]], [[Corinna Brown]], [[Kizzy Edgell]], [[Tobie Donovan]], [[Jenny Walser]], [[Rhea Norwood]], [[Leila Khan (actress)|Leila Khan]], [[Sebastian Croft]], Cormac Hyde-Corrin and [[Olivia Colman]]. As the characters grow older, the series expands to explore sexuality, gender identity, mental health, intimacy and early adulthood.

Produced by [[See-Saw Films]], ''Heartstopper'' was adapted for television after the company acquired the screen rights in 2019. Oseman wrote every episode. [[Euros Lyn]] directed the first two series, with Andy Newbery directing the third. Three series of eight episodes each were released between 2022 and 2024; the first premiered on 22 April 2022, followed by the second on 3 August 2023 and the third on 3 October 2024. In April 2025, Netflix announced that the screen adaptation would conclude with a feature-length finale film, ''[[Heartstopper Forever]]'', which was released on 17 July 2026.

The series has received critical acclaim, particularly for Oseman's writing, the performances of Connor and Locke, faithfulness to the source material and its warm and affirming portrayal of LGBTQ+ youth. It won the [[Children's and Family Emmy Award for Outstanding Young Teen Series|Children's and Family Emmy Award for Outstanding Young Teen Series]], while Connor, Locke and Oseman also won Children's and Family Emmy Awards for their work on the programme. ''Heartstopper'' also received [[GLAAD Media Award]]s for outstanding kids and family programming, as well as honours from [[BAFTA Cymru]], the [[Royal Television Society]], the [[Dorian Awards]], the [[Kidscreen Awards]] and the [[MTV Movie & TV Awards]].

''Heartstopper'' entered Netflix's Global Top 10 shortly after release, helped boost sales of Oseman's books, and increased streams and chart activity for songs featured on its soundtrack. Commentators identified the series as part of a broader shift towards more joyful and hopeful LGBTQ+ television, while Nick's bisexual storyline was widely highlighted as an important example of bisexual representation on screen.

selected_sections.heading: Premise
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
''Heartstopper'' follows teenagers [[Charlie Spring]] and [[Nick Nelson (Heartstopper)|Nick Nelson]], whose friendship at Truham Grammar School develops into a romantic relationship. Charlie, who was [[Outing|outed]] as [[gay]] before the events of the story, contends with bullying and the effects of a secret relationship with Ben Hope, while Nick begins to question his sexuality. Their story unfolds alongside those of their friends Tao Xu, Elle Argent and Isaac Henderson, as well as Higgs Girls School students Tara Jones and Darcy Olsson. Elle, a [[transgender]] girl, has transferred to Higgs, and the wider friendship group navigates changing relationships, identity and [[Coming out|coming out]].

As the characters grow older, the series expands to explore mental health, intimacy and the uncertainties of early adulthood. Later storylines include Nick's gradual coming out as [[Bisexuality|bisexual]], Charlie's treatment for [[anorexia nervosa]] and [[obsessive–compulsive disorder]], Tao and Elle's developing relationship, Isaac's understanding of himself as [[Aromantic asexual|aromantic and asexual]], and Darcy's exploration of their [[non-binary]] identity.

selected_sections.heading: Premise
selected_sections.raw_wikitext: ''Young Royals'' follows Prince Wilhelm of Sweden in the prestigious [[boarding school]] Hillerska as he develops a relationship with his classmate Simon. Under the constant view of the public eye, the series depicts how their relationship affects everyone around them.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Young Royals - TV Series |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt14664414/ |access-date=2023-07-28 |website=IMDb}}</ref> The series addresses [[homophobia]], [[mental illness]], [[eating disorder]]s, [[infidelity]], [[Addiction|drug addiction]], [[stalking]], [[abuse]], [[internalized racism]], [[autism]], the relationship between [[social class]]es, and [[constitutional monarchy]].

selected_sections.heading: Viewership
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
The first season made it to the top 10 in 12 countries and was streamed for more than 9.8 million hours worldwide. In the first week after its release, the first season was ranked the eighth most streamed non-English language series on Netflix worldwide.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://top10.netflix.com/tv-non-english?week=2021-07-11 | title=Netflix Top 10 - Global }}</ref>

The second season made it to the top 10 in 26 countries and was streamed more than 18 million hours in the first week. During this week, the second season was ranked the third most streamed non-English language series on Netflix worldwide.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Top 10 Non-English Shows on Netflix Right Now - Netflix Tudum |url=https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10/tv-non-english?week=2022-11-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124101030/https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10/tv-non-english?week=2022-11-06 |archive-date=24 January 2025 |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=Netflix Tudum |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

The third season's first five episodes made it to the top 10 in 47 countries and was streamed more than 11.5 million hours by its first week. During this week, the third season was the fifth most streamed non-English language series on Netflix worldwide.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Top 10 Non-English Shows on Netflix Right Now - Netflix Tudum |url=https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10/tv-non-english?week=2024-03-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241228091843/https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10/tv-non-english?week=2024-03-17 |archive-date=28 December 2024 |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=Netflix Tudum |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> The finale kept the show afloat in top 10 in ninth place, garnering 7.5 million hours watched by its second week.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-07 |title=Top 10 non-English streamed shows |url=https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10/tv-non-english?week=2024-03-24 |website=Netflix Tudum}}</ref>

selected_sections.heading: Critical response
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
''Young Royals'' received critical acclaim and positive responses from audiences. On the review aggregation website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the series holds an approval rating of 100%, based on five reviews, with an average rating of 8.3/10.<ref name="RottenTomatoes">{{cite web |title=Young Royals: Season 1 |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/young_royals/s01 |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date=15 October 2022 |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]}}</ref> It has been praised for its fidelity to real life in casting teenagers for teenage roles and showing skin textures with blemishes.<ref name="Digital Spy">{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a36937479/young-royals-gay-sex-queer-lgbtq|title=''Young Royals'' does this one thing better than other teen shows like Élite or Riverdale|last=Opie|first=David|date=6 July 2021|website=Digital Spy|access-date=18 July 2021}}</ref><ref name="Radio Times review">{{cite magazine|last=Carr|first=Flora|date=28 June 2021|title=''Young Royals'' review: Netflix's predictable but heartfelt Swedish teen drama leans into the intensity of first love|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/young-royals-review-netflix|journal=Radio Times}}</ref> Some critics and audiences compared the series favourably to similar shows such as ''[[Elite (TV series)|Elite]]'', ''[[Gossip Girl]]'', ''[[The Crown (TV series)|The Crown]]'' and ''[[Skam (TV series)|Skam]]''.<ref name="Radio Times review" /><ref name="Digital Spy" />

David Opie of ''[[Digital Spy]]'' praised ''Young Royals'' for "cast[ing] actors who actually look the age they are supposed to be playing" and "portray[ing] teenage life with some much-needed authenticity". He described the series as "an updated version of the classic Cinderella story" and concluded that the series "excels most [...] when it comes to the central romance between Wilhelm and Simon".<ref name="Digital Spy" /> TV critic Flora Carr of ''[[Radio Times]]'' in a review of the first two episodes described the series as "predictable but heartfelt". She criticised the series' "checklist of teen-romance visuals" and "the plot's reliance on characters like August", but ultimately concluded that "the authentically teenage cast may also prove a breath of fresh air" for younger viewers.<ref name="Radio Times review" />

For the second season, Dieter Osswald of Swiss lifestyle magazine ''Display'' wrote: "Like stand-up characters, the separated lovers defy their fate and fight for their love. The chemistry between Edvin Ryding as the insecure prince and Omar Rudberg as the sensitive singer works even better than in the first season. Fans of creep August aka Malte Gardinger can look forward to bigger appearances with a strongly expanded role - including a naked phone call with the royal family."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prince Charming aus Schweden {{!}} DISPLAY-Magazin |date=November 2022 |url=https://www.display-magazin.ch/prince-charming-aus-schweden/ |access-date=1 November 2022 |language=de-DE}}</ref>

For the third season, Germany's popular site ''Queer.de'' wrote: "Convinces with plenty of emotional drama, surprising twists, and more political stance. Are you still watching? Or are you already crying?"<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oßwald |first=Dieter |title="Young Royals": Mehr Knutschzeit für Wille und Simon |url=https://www.queer.de/detail.php?article_id=48780 |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=queer.de |language=de-DE}}</ref>

'''''One Day''''' is a British [[romantic drama]] [[Limited-run series|limited series]] based on the [[One Day (novel)|2009 novel]] by [[David Nicholls (writer)|David Nicholls]] as well as the [[One Day (2011 film)|2011 film adaptation]]. It follows the 14-year relationship of Emma Morley and Dexter Mayhew, who meet at a graduation [[Ball (dance event)|ball]] after graduating from the [[University of Edinburgh]], and stars [[Leo Woodall]] and [[Ambika Mod]] in the lead roles.

Premiering on 8 February 2024 on [[Netflix]], it received critical acclaim and was the most-watched series globally during the week of 12 February, with 9.9 million views.

selected_sections.heading: Reception
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
The series received critical acclaim and was the most-watched series globally during the week of 12 February 2024, with 9.9 million views.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seitz |first=Loree |date=20 February 2024 |title=One Day, Love is Blind Season 6 Lure Netflix TV Viewers |url=https://www.thewrap.com/one-day-love-is-blind-netflix-tv-viewership/ |access-date=22 February 2024 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US}}</ref>

selected_sections.heading: Plot
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
In [[Seoul]], [[South Korea]], in 1999, Na Young and Hae Sung are 12-year-old classmates who develop feelings for each other and go on a playdate set up by their parents. Shortly thereafter, Na Young's family immigrates to [[Canada]] and the two lose contact. Na Young changes her name to Nora.

In 2011, Hae Sung has finished his [[Conscription in South Korea|military service]] and Nora has moved to [[New York City]]. While calling her mother, Nora discovers on [[Facebook]] that Hae Sung had posted that he was looking for Na Young, unaware of her name change. They reconnect through video calls but are unable to visit each other, as Nora is about to attend a writer's retreat in [[Montauk, New York|Montauk]] and Hae Sung is moving to China for a Mandarin language exchange. Eventually, Nora tells Hae Sung they should stop talking for a while, as she wants to focus on her writing and life in New York.

At her retreat, Nora meets Arthur Zaturansky and they fall in love, at one point discussing the [[Korean Buddhism|Buddhist]]-derived concept of {{Transliteration|ko|inyeon}} ({{lang|ko|인연}}, [[Pratītyasamutpāda|dependent origination]]), how a relationship between two souls in the present life is influenced by interactions in thousands of past lives. Hae Sung also meets a woman, whom he begins to date.

In 2023, Arthur and Nora are married and living in New York. Hae Sung, no longer with his girlfriend, travels to visit Nora. Arthur wonders if he is a roadblock in their love story, suggesting to Nora that, if another man with similar appeal had met her at the same time, Nora would have married him to secure a [[green card]] for U.S. residency. He also expresses anxiety about cultural barriers in their relationship, highlighting Nora's habit of sleep-talking in Korean: "you dream in a language that I can't understand." Nora reassures Arthur that she loves him.

The next night, the three go out to a speakeasy. Initially, Nora translates between the two men, but eventually speaks with Hae Sung exclusively in Korean. He wonders what they were to each other in their past lives, and what would have happened if she had never left Korea and they had continued their relationship. When Nora goes to the bathroom, Hae Sung apologizes to Arthur for speaking alone with Nora, but Arthur says he is glad to have met him.

They return to Arthur and Nora's apartment. Hae Sung invites them to visit him in Korea and calls an [[Uber]]. Nora waits with him, and the two exchange long looks at each other until the car arrives. Hae Sung says that perhaps they are, at that moment, experiencing a past life, and asks Nora what their relationship will be in their next life. She says she does not know. Hae Sung says, "I'll see you then." He leaves in the car and she walks back to her apartment, crying into Arthur's arms.

selected_sections.heading: Critical response
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
<!--UPDATE the access-date of the source that you used when you update these figures.-->{{RT prose |score=95 |count=319 |ref=yes |access-date=September 4, 2025 |consensus=A remarkable debut for writer-director Celine Song, ''Past Lives'' uses the bonds between its sensitively sketched central characters to support trenchant observations on the human condition.}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 94 out of 100, based on 52 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''Past Lives'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/past-lives |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=March 8, 2024 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref>

Manola Darghis, in ''[[The New York Times]]'', compared the film to French romantic cinema, complimenting its restraint in the presentation of its main themes, and writing: "The movie's modesty—its intimacy, human scale, humble locations and lack of visual oomph—is one of its strengths. The characters live in homes that are pleasant yet ordinary, the kind that you can imagine hanging out in, the kind you want to hang out in. There are few big, look-at-me details, though you might notice a poster for [[Jacques Rivette]]’s 1974 classic ''[[Céline and Julie Go Boating]]'' in Nora’s father’s home office in Seoul."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dargis |first=Manohla |author-link=Manohla Dargis |date=June 1, 2023 |title='Past Lives' Review: Longing for a Future |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/06/01/movies/past-lives-review.html |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |access-date=September 4, 2026}}</ref> In ''[[The Guardian]]'', [[Peter Bradshaw]] praised the film highly, referencing existing comparisons to the works of [[Richard Linklater]], [[Noah Baumbach]], and [[Greta Gerwig]], and himself likening the film to [[Wong Kar-wai]]'s "[[In the Mood for Love]]". He wrote: "''Past Lives'' is a glorious date movie, and a movie for every occasion, too. As ever with films like this, there is an auxiliary pleasure in wondering how much of her own past life Song has used. It's a must-see."<ref name="Bradshaw 2023">{{cite web |last=Bradshaw |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Bradshaw |date=September 6, 2023 |title=Past Lives review – a must-see story of lost loves, childhood crushes and changing identities |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/sep/06/past-lives-review-a-must-see-story-of-lost-loves-childhood-crushes-and-changing-identities |website=The Guardian |language=en-GB |access-date=September 14, 2023}}</ref>

Filmmaker [[Daniels (directors)|Daniel Scheinert]], who co-directed A24's ''[[Everything Everywhere All at Once]]'' with Daniel Kwan, praised the film, saying: "It's remarkable, the way [Celine Song] pushed past the story of 'picking mister right' and the story of 'fighting to win the girl' and somehow brought her audience to this painfully relatable heartbreak on the other side of those stories. I'm inspired by it. And mystified by how the filmmaking team did it. But when I was lucky enough to see a Q&A and have some brunch with Celine, I saw how curious and thoughtful and passionate and charmingly bossy she was, and I was instantly convinced that this movie was no accident. It's a smart, confident, unique poem because Celine is a smart, confident, unique poet."<ref>{{cite web |date=December 13, 2023 |title=16 Directors Praise 2023's Best Films: Alfonso Cuarón on 'Killers of the Flower Moon,' Jane Campion on 'Priscilla' and More |url=https://variety.com/lists/directors-best-films-2023/past-lives-2/ |website=Variety |language=en-US |access-date=September 4, 2026}}</ref> Filmmaker [[Christopher Nolan]] also praised the film and named it one of his favorites, calling it "subtle in a beautiful sort of way".<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Kluger |first=Jeffrey |date=January 29, 2024 |title=How Christopher Nolan Found Intimacy on a Grand Scale |url=https://time.com/6589108/christopher-nolan-oppenheimer-oscars-interview/ |magazine=Time |language=en-US |access-date=January 31, 2024 |archive-date=March 6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240306180405/https://time.com/6589108/christopher-nolan-oppenheimer-oscars-interview/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> Other filmmakers, such as [[Allison Anders]], [[Reinaldo Marcus Green]], [[Andrew Haigh]], [[Rich Peppiatt]], and [[Zoe Lister-Jones]] cited it as among their favorite films of 2023.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 31, 2023 |title=38 Directors Pick Their Favorite Films of 2023 |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-best-movies-tv-2023|website=IndieWire}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Kneecap Director Rich Peppiatt Top Ten Feature Films of 2024 |url=https://directorsnotes.com/2024/12/30/rich-peppiatt-top-ten-2024/ |website=Director's Notes |date=December 30, 2024 |access-date=September 4, 2026}}</ref>

How does someone choose between two lovers, one that represents the most fruitful days of her youth, and the other someone she has grown to love as part of her reality? Celine Song examines these critical conversations through the perspective of an immigrant story."<ref>{{cite web |last=Gaughan |first=Liam |date=September 28, 2023 |title='Don't be so eager to be offended.' the 20 Best Drama Movies of the 2020s So Far, Ranked |url=https://collider.com/best-drama-movies-2020s/ |website=Collider |language=en-US |access-date=September 4, 2026}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[IndieWire]]'' included it on its list of the "Best American Independent Movies of the 21st Century" and in 2025 ranked it 40th on its list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 2020s (So Far)."<ref name="Foreman & Erbland 2024">{{cite web |last1=Foreman |first1=Alison |last2=Erbland |first2=Kate |date=July 3, 2024 |title=The Best American Independent Films of the 21st Century |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/best-american-indie-movies-21st-century |website=IndieWire |language=en-US |access-date=September 4, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The 100 Best Movies of the 2020s (So Far) |url=https://www.indiewire.com/lists/best-movies-2020s/ |website=IndieWire |language=en-US |date=June 16, 2025 |access-date=June 23, 2025}}</ref> ''[[Looper (website)|Looper]]'' also named it the "Best [[PG-13]] Movie of All Time," calling it "a master class in the art of subtlety while evoking complex human emotions. '''''Nobody Wants This''''' is an American [[romantic comedy]] television series created by [[Erin Foster]] which premiered on [[Netflix]] on September 26, 2024 and stars [[Kristen Bell]], [[Adam Brody]], [[Justine Lupe]], [[Timothy Simons]] and [[Jackie Tohn]].

''Nobody Wants This'' focuses on the unlikely relationship between an outspoken, [[agnosticism|agnostic]] woman and a handsome young [[Jewish]] [[rabbi]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hudgins |first=Ryan |date=2024-09-30 |title=What Kristen Bell and Adam Brody Have Said About Playing Younger in 'Nobody Wants This' |url=https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/kristen-bell-adam-brodys-quotes-about-their-ages-in-nobody-wants-this/ |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=Us Weekly |language=en-US}}</ref> The series was met with positive reviews from critics and also received several accolades, with the first season earning three nominations at the [[77th Primetime Emmy Awards]], for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series|Outstanding Comedy Series]] and outstanding acting for both Bell and Brody. In November 2025, the series was renewed for a third season which is scheduled to premiere on October 22, 2026.<!--Per WP:CITELEAD, references are not needed in the lead if it is sourced in the body of the article.-->

selected_sections.heading: Premise
selected_sections.raw_wikitext: ''Nobody Wants This'' follows the love-at-first-sight relationship between a young American rabbi, Noah ([[Adam Brody]]), and an irascible [[agnosticism|agnostic]] woman, Joanne ([[Kristen Bell]]). Joanne co-hosts a podcast, with her sister, Morgan ([[Justine Lupe]]) about relationships; Noah, who hopes to be promoted to chief rabbi of his [[synagogue]], has just ended his long term relationship with a Jewish woman.

selected_sections.heading: Critical response
Season 1
selected_sections.raw_wikitext:
On the [[review aggregator]] website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the first season holds a 95% approval rating for the first season with an average rating of 7.8/10, based on 56 critic reviews. The website's critics consensus reads, "Contrary to its title, ''Nobody Wants This'' proves to be a welcome binge thanks to [[Kristen Bell]] and [[Adam Brody]]'s irresistible chemistry and some thoughtful considerations of interfaith romance."<ref name="RTS1">{{Cite Rotten Tomatoes|id=nobody_wants_this|title=Nobody Wants This|type=tv|season=1|access-date=October 6, 2024|publisher_hide=y}}{{cbignore}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a weighted average, assigned a score of 73 out of 100 based on 27 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="MCS1">{{Cite Metacritic|id=nobody-wants-this|title=Nobody Wants This|type=tv|season=1|access-date=September 28, 2024|publisher_hide=y}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

''[[Glamour (magazine)|Glamour]]'' senior editor Jessica Radloff published an essay stating that the show's Jewish characters "come off as controlling, marriage-hungry women who want to plan dinner parties and alienate anyone who doesn't share those same dreams." She also took issue with the use of ''[[shiksa]]'' in the first episode "Pilot".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Radloff |first=Jessica |date=September 27, 2024 |title=Netflix's Nobody Wants This and the Persistent Jewish Stereotype |url=https://www.glamour.com/story/netflixs-nobody-wants-this-and-the-persistent-jewish-stereotype |access-date=October 2, 2024 |website=Glamour |language=en-US}}</ref> In response, Foster has stated "I think we need positive Jewish stories right now. I think it's interesting when people focus on, 'Oh, this is a stereotype of Jewish people,' when you have a rabbi as the lead. A hot, cool, young rabbi who smokes weed. That's the antithesis of how people view a Jewish rabbi, right?"<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zack |date=October 1, 2024 |title='Nobody Wants This' Criticized for 'Stereotypical' and 'Mean-Spirited' Jewish Characters; Creator Says Netflix Series Aims to 'Shed Positive Light on Jewish Culture' |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/nobody-wants-this-backlash-jewish-women-netflix-1236161391/ |access-date=October 2, 2024 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-date=October 2, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002060133/https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/nobody-wants-this-backlash-jewish-women-netflix-1236161391/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

''[[The Independent]]''{{'}}s Kate Rosseinsky gave the show a score of 4/5, claiming that although there are a "few obvious tropes", there are still many less predictable comedic moments that can be "sometimes hilariously, slightly relatable."<ref name=":0" /> ''[[The Guardian]]'' TV critic Lucy Mangan rated the show 5/5 stars, stating, "Everybody will want this". She feels that there are real emotional stakes and that the majorly opposing cultures of the two main characters are "genuine problems," and although they are blocking paths of happiness with no clear answers, she will be with them to the bitter end.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Mangan |first=Lucy |date=September 26, 2024 |title='Nobody Wants This review – Kristen Bell and Adam Brody's joyous romcom is as funny as When Harry Met Sally' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2024/sep/26/nobody-wants-this-review-kristen-bell-and-adam-brodys-joyous-romcom-is-as-funny-as-when-harry-met-sally |access-date=October 5, 2024 |website=The Guardian |language=en-US}}</ref>

selected_sections.heading: Season 2
selected_sections.raw_wikitext: On Rotten Tomatoes, the second season has a 79% approval rating, based on 52 critic reviews. The website's critics consensus states, "In its second outing, ''Nobody Wants This''{{'}} sharp humor and warmly chaotic ensemble keep it an engaging and emotionally observant rom-com that still charms even as it stumbles."<ref name="RTS2">{{Cite Rotten Tomatoes|id=nobody_wants_this|title=Nobody Wants This|type=tv|season=2|access-date=October 30, 2025|publisher_hide=y}}{{cbignore}}</ref> On Metacritic, it has a weighted average score of 64 out of 100 based on 22 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="MCS2">{{Cite Metacritic|id=nobody-wants-this|title=Nobody Wants This|type=tv|season=2|access-date=October 30, 2025|publisher_hide=y}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
